trigger_condition: ModelStatus type uses 'enabled' but spec and API contract use 'active'
potential_consequence: Type diverges from API contract; 'active' values never match ModelStatus literal
API response value 'active' is not assignable; store default 'enabled' also mismatches spec

trigger_condition: Default fallback stores 'enabled' but spec requires default to be 'active'
potential_consequence: Absent-status models stored as 'enabled'; catalog filter compares against 'deprecated' so they pass, but type contract and spec are violated

trigger_condition: Filter nullish-coalesces status to 'enabled' to compare against 'deprecated'
potential_consequence: If spec's default 'active' is ever enforced, the coalesce to 'enabled' is redundant dead code; currently harmless but misleading

trigger_condition: OptionMeta renders isPremium and isDeprecated without separator between them
potential_consequence: A model that is both premium and deprecated renders 'PremiumDeprecated' with no visual separator

trigger_condition: OPTION_ID_RECOMMENDED item rendered without status; defaultModel may be deprecated
guard_snippet: pass recommended={true} status={defaultModel.status} to ModelOptionRow for the recommended slot
potential_consequence: A deprecated default model shown in 'Recommended' slot without Deprecated label

trigger_condition: ArrowUp/ArrowDown navigation stops on disabled items; user cannot skip past them
guard_snippet: skip disabled indices in the ArrowDown/ArrowUp handler before calling setHighlightedIndex
potential_consequence: Keyboard navigation halts at a deprecated item; Enter press at that index silently no-ops

trigger_condition: disabled button has role='option' with no aria-disabled attribute
guard_snippet: aria-disabled={item.disabled ?? false} alongside the disabled prop
potential_consequence: Screen readers see a focusable option with no accessible disabled state; ARIA pattern violated

trigger_condition: deprecatedCount counts all deprecated models, not only those matching current filters
guard_snippet: const deprecatedCount = filtered.filter((m) => m.status === 'deprecated').length (or use llmModels consistently and document intent)
potential_consequence: Summary line says N deprecated while none are visible even with showDeprecated=true + provider filter active

trigger_condition: Status cell renders empty (no element) for 'enabled' and 'disabled' — 'disabled' is a live enum value
guard_snippet: add an else branch or chip for status === 'disabled' if backend ever surfaces it
potential_consequence: A 'disabled' model shows no Status badge despite having a non-default lifecycle status

trigger_condition: disabled: status === 'deprecated' also fires for status === 'disabled'; spec says treat both the same display-wise
potential_consequence: 'disabled' status models remain selectable in assistant form selector despite spec intent

trigger_condition: disabled: m.status === 'deprecated' does not cover status === 'disabled'
potential_consequence: 'disabled' status models remain selectable in chat prompt selector

trigger_condition: Test asserts '.p-disabled' class but SearchableCombobox sets HTML disabled, not a CSS class
guard_snippet: assert button[disabled] or use toBeDisabled() matcher instead of class-name sniff
potential_consequence: Test may pass vacuously or target wrong element; real disabled state unverified

trigger_condition: Test asserts '.p-disabled' class; same mismatch as LLMSelector.test.tsx
guard_snippet: assert toBeDisabled() on the rendered option button instead
potential_consequence: Test does not actually verify the option is disabled; regression possible
